name: Edward Said
role: Palestinian-American literary critic and public intellectual (1935–2003)
summary: Edward Said was a Columbia professor of literature whose Orientalism founded postcolonial studies and who became the best-known voice of the Palestinian cause in the United States. He criticised empire, American policy in the Arab world, Oslo and Arab authoritarianism, and later argued for a single binational state with equal citizenship, while condemning attacks on civilians.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: Said says Israel bears moral responsibility for the nakba and that Palestinian rights have never been admitted.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Said writes that international law, including the UN Charter, gives a people under military occupation the right to resist by any means, while calling suicide bombings in Tel Aviv useless and unacceptable.

arms-reduction.rationale: Said criticises huge arms purchases in the Arab world in place of human development and the rising American defence budget.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Said calls attacks on civilians criminal, whether by Israel's army or by the 9/11 killers, and says the PLO's terrorist actions hurt its cause.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Said calls the idea that empire is benign and necessary a self-serving imperial perspective that treats subjects as people whose fate others decide.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Said condemns imperial rule as domination and plunder behind a claimed mission, and denies that its subjects' views matter to the rulers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said asks how citizens can resist the blandishments of companies like Halliburton and Boeing and of lobbies over American policy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Said condemns the American terror war for consigning laws, constitutional rights and habeas corpus to the rubbish bin.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said calls for equality for all, one person one vote, and full citizenship for Palestinians in Israel.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said calls the homogenising of societies into a Jewish state or purely Arab states a tragedy of identity politics with terrible results.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Said attacks regime change by powerful states and American imposition of its views on the Arab world.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Said calls the Jews a people with a history of persecution and genocide and says Jews are justified in feeling the Holocaust as their own.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said rejects the view that Arabs and Muslims belong to sealed-off civilisations unfit for self-determination, and argues the Arab world lacks democracy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Said rejects the 'Islam versus the West' scheme as a cartoon, and says Muslims are now at the centre of the West.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said argues for a binational state with equal citizenship and calls Israel's character as the state of the Jewish people, not of its citizens, a source of inferior rights.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Said endorses a critique of absolutists who reduce Islam to a penal code stripped of humanism, and calls theocracy a dead end alongside nationalism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said argues no one has proved privatisation and 'free' enterprise improved electricity, transport or prisons, wants roads and water run by the public sector, and calls the American-style globalisation where the market is king something to resist.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Said calls the Iraq war unnecessary and rigged and says oil and Israel's interests drove American military policy.

national-mission.rationale: Said says every empire tells itself it has a mission to educate and liberate, and asks what it means to democratise a country by occupying it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said counts the deferral of an open press and free universities as a cost of Arab militarised nationalism.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Said praises armed Palestinian resistance to the occupation as defence, but calls suicide bombing and terrorism harmful and useless.

population-transfer.rationale: Said condemns the 1948 expulsions and the Israeli politicians who advocate transfer, and speaks of ethnic cleansing as an injustice.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said condemns the discriminatory legal system in Israel as virtual apartheid and says separation cannot work, as it failed under apartheid.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: Said treats UN resolutions 242 and 194 as valid against facts imposed by power and calls for total Israeli withdrawal from the territories taken in 1967.

refugee-return.rationale: Said invokes UN Resolution 194 on return and insists on restitution and return for the Palestinians driven out in 1948.

religious-nation.rationale: Said calls a state of one religious people an anomaly of nationalism and theocracy and wants a secular citizenship campaign.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Said denounces the expulsion of whole communities in 1948 and ethnic cleansing as disasters and injustices.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Said argues the decades of occupation damage must not be wiped away, demands restitution and floats a South African-style truth commission.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Said describes Israel's war on the Palestinians as colonial and the creation of Israel as a conquest that destroyed Palestinian society.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said condemns Arab regimes' campaign against dissenters with prison, torture and executions as wasteful and cruel.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said condemns conquest of land by force, from the 1948 conquest of Palestine to settlement expansion and imperial rule.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Said condemns Israel as the only state where torture is legally justified in interrogation and denounces the torture at Khiam prison.

unions-good.rationale: Said lists trade unions among the Palestinian interests that sustained society and should anchor reform, and decries American labour unions under constant attack.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said names the absence of health insurance among the ways the United States has dismantled the attributes of the welfare state compared with other industrial democracies.

universal-morality.rationale: Said says the world is better understood through universal principles of justice and injustice than through civilisational labels.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Scholarship describes Said as an engaged public intellectual who spoke truth to power for decades on Palestine.

notes: Said held no office, so his articles and speeches stand as his own words. Themes searched: Palestine and Israel (Oslo, Camp David, the second intifada, binationalism), empire and the Iraq war, 9/11 and Islam, Arab authoritarianism, violence and intellectuals. He wrote almost nothing on economic policy, taxes, welfare, technology or ecology in the sources read, so those statements stay null. His 1999 shift from a two-state to a binational view is recorded where it bears on an answer.
